en.t: The architect was still not satisfied with this.

units.source_text: 他还在法水院西侧架起一座形似钓段的小巧玲政的漱清亭。

en.t: He also built, on the west side of the Hosui-in, a small and elegant Sosei-tei shaped like a fishing platform.

units.source_text: 似乎要打破均衡，他就将其赌注押在一切美的力量方面。

en.t: As if trying to break the balance, he staked everything on the power of beauty.

units.source_text: 对这建筑物来说，漱清亭是反抗形而上学的。

en.t: For this building, the Sosei-tei was a rebellion against metaphysics.

units.source_text: 虽然它决不是长长地伸向地面，却看似是从金阁的中心通达到任何的地方。

en.t: Although it by no means stretched far down toward the ground, it seemed to lead from the center of the Golden Pavilion to anywhere at all.

units.source_text: 漱清亭像一只展翅欲飞的鸟，如今张开了翅膀，正从这建筑物向地面上，向一切当今世界的东西道逃。

en.t: Like a bird spreading its wings to fly, the Sosei-tei now opened its wings and seemed to flee from this building toward the ground, toward everything of the present world.

units.source_text: 这意味着是从规定世界的秩序向无规定的东西，甚至可能是向官能过渡的桥。

en.t: This meant a bridge passing from the order of a defined world toward what was undefined, perhaps even toward sensuality.

units.source_text: 金阁的精灵就是从这座形似半截桥的激清事开始，完成三层的楼阁，然后又从这座桥通达的。

en.t: The spirit of the Golden Pavilion began from this structure, like half a bridge, completed the three-storied pavilion, and then passed out again through that bridge.

units.source_text: 因为漂荡在地面上的巨大的官能的力量，虽是建筑金阁的潜在力g的源泉，但这种力量在完全建立起秩序、完成美丽的三层楼阁之后，再也无法忍耐居住于此，

en.t: Because the immense sensual force drifting over the ground, though it was the source of the latent power that built the Golden Pavilion, could no longer bear to dwell there after it had fully established order and completed the beautiful three-storied pavilion,

units.source_text: 就只好顺着漱清亭再次向池面、向无垠的官能的荡漾、向故乡通达了。

en.t: and so it had no choice but to follow the Sosei-tei back toward the surface of the pond, toward the boundless rippling of sensuality, toward its homeland.
Apart from this, there was no other way.
This was something I often pondered.

units.source_text: 每逢眺望弥漫在镜湖池上的朝雾夕霭的时候，我就思忖着那里才是筑起金阁的巨大的官能力量的所在。

en.t: Whenever I gazed at the morning mist or evening haze spreading over Kyoko Pond, I would think that there, indeed, was the dwelling place of the immense sensual force that had raised the Golden Pavilion.
